name: VA Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
description: Medically necessary changes to a veteran’s primary home, including permanent ramps, accessible bathrooms and widened access. Some non-service-connected needs can qualify.
next_step: Ask your VA care team for a clinical review and contact your VA medical facility’s Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service. Confirm your remaining lifetime benefit and obtain the HISA application checklist.
constraints: HISA excludes portable ramps, stair glides, new construction and routine home repairs. VA determines eligibility, medical necessity and the available benefit. Prepare VA Form 10-0103, a VA-written or approved prescription, owner authorization (notarized for renters), an itemized estimate and a before photograph.

name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant
description: A housing grant route for veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities.

constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

name: VA Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) grant

name: VA Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA)
description: Changes to a family member’s home where a qualifying veteran or service member is living temporarily.
next_step: Ask VA about TRA if you qualify for SAH or SHA and are temporarily living in a family member’s home.
constraints: TRA requires SAH or SHA eligibility; it is not a general temporary-housing or renter grant.

name: Ohio waiver home modifications
description: Approved home modifications can include ramps, grab bars, doorway widening and bathroom changes under qualifying home and community-based programs.
next_step: If enrolled, ask your waiver case manager to assess the modification and authorize it in your service plan. Otherwise ask your county aging agency or Ohio Medicaid for screening.
constraints: Medicaid coverage alone does not establish access to this service. Applicable program enrollment, assessed need, service-plan authorization, owner consent and provider requirements apply.
organization: Ohio Department of Medicaid / Ohio Department of Aging

name: Developmental disability waiver home adaptations
description: Environmental accessibility adaptations may support eligible people enrolled in Ohio Individual Options or Level One waivers.
next_step: Ask your county board of developmental disabilities service and support administrator about assessment and authorization in the individual service plan.
constraints: DD eligibility alone does not establish waiver enrollment or funding. Adaptations must meet waiver rules; new home construction and residential-facility modifications are excluded.

name: USDA rural home repair loans and grants
description: Section 504 assistance for qualifying very-low-income rural homeowners; grants help qualifying older homeowners remove health and safety hazards.
next_step: Use USDA’s Ohio program page to check the property and income requirements and contact a home loan specialist about an accessibility project.
constraints: Grants require age 62 or older and additional eligibility conditions. Loans and grants have different rules. This is not a statewide entitlement or a general renter program.

name: Ohio HOME Choice: returning to the community
description: Transition coordination for eligible Ohioans moving from a long-term-care facility to a community setting.
next_step: Ask the facility discharge planner and HOME Choice staff to coordinate housing, supports and accessibility needs before the move.
constraints: Medicaid and other eligibility requirements apply. HOME Choice is a transition route, not an automatic ramp grant.

name: Medicare questions: OSHIIP counseling
description: Personalized Medicare and related health insurance counseling for Ohioans.
next_step: Call OSHIIP with questions about Medicare coverage, plan choices or costs. Ask which counseling or financial-help screening fits your situation.
constraints: Medicare eligibility is separate from age alone. Counseling does not guarantee enrollment or payment for a service.

name: Vision loss: Independent Living Older Blind program
description: Skills, tools and support to help qualifying older Ohioans with significant vision impairment live more independently.
next_step: Call OOD and ask for the Independent Living Older Blind program. Describe the daily activities affected by vision loss and ask for an eligibility assessment.
constraints: Age 55+ and additional program criteria apply. OOD assesses eligibility and feasible independent living goals; age or a diagnosis alone is insufficient.

name: Memory loss and dementia: 24/7 support
description: Free, confidential dementia information, caregiver support and referrals to local community resources.
next_step: Call the Alzheimer’s Association helpline for care planning, local support groups and caregiver guidance. Seek medical evaluation for new memory concerns.
constraints: The helpline provides support and referrals; it does not replace clinical assessment or emergency services.

name: Hearing and speech: Ohio Relay
description: Communication assistance for telephone calls involving people who are deaf, hard of hearing, deafblind or have a speech disability.
next_step: Dial 711 or use the Ohio Relay service instructions to choose a communication method that fits your needs.
constraints: Relay is a communication service, not a hearing aid grant or medical assessment.

name: Disability independence: find a Center for Independent Living
description: Find independent living organizations to ask about disability-related navigation, skills, peer support and advocacy.
next_step: Use the Ohio SILC directory and ask the center whether it serves your county and which services are available.
constraints: Center coverage is not universal across Ohio counties; confirm the service area before relying on a referral.

name: PASSPORT: ask about help at home
description: A screening route for older Ohioans who may qualify for Medicaid-funded home and community-based care.
next_step: Ask the county aging agency for PASSPORT screening and an assessment of care needs, financial eligibility and available services.
constraints: Age 60+ at enrollment, Medicaid eligibility, qualifying level of care, safe community living and additional enrollment criteria apply. An assessment or diagnosis does not guarantee an available waiver slot.

name: American Legion: find a local post
description: Official post lookup for community connections and identifying public contacts to share the guide with.
next_step: Search the official directory for your town or ZIP code. Confirm the post’s public phone or email and ask who handles community partnerships.
constraints: A local post is not automatically an accredited claims office or a funding provider. Confirm its services, membership or visitor rules, accessibility and current contact details.
